title: Why Good Rapport With Students Is A Choice You Make Every Day -you-make-every-day/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin argues that good rapport with students isn't a personality trait, a skill, or a matter of spending extra time chatting — it's a daily choice to like every student regardless of their behavior. He warns that negative feelings toward students, even unspoken ones, leak out through body language, tone, and word choice, and children are especially attuned to noticing it. He describes a virtuous cycle: choosing to like students consciously, even the most difficult ones, causes them to like the teacher back, trust them, and behave differently. Practically, he recommends smiling at every student and treating them like your best-behaved students from day one and every day after. He acknowledges this can require deliberate effort on hard days but insists it's foundational to influence, motivation, and job satisfaction.
points: Rapport is described as a choice, not an innate skill or a function of extra time spent with students.
Negative feelings about students leak out through body language, tone, and word choice even when unspoken.
Choosing to consistently like every student — including difficult ones — creates a virtuous cycle where they begin liking and trusting the teacher back.
Practical rapport-building starts with smiling at every student and treating them like your best-behaved students from day one.
quotes: Because when you dislike or resent any one or more of your students, they’ll know it . It’s something you can’t hide.
So, while the key to building influential rapport is nothing more than being consistently pleasant , it’s only possible if you choose to like your students.

And here’s the amazing thing: Once you commit yourself to liking every student and seeing only the best in them—no matter who they are or what they’ve done in the past—they become not so unlikable after all.
So, practically, on the first day of school and thereafter, make it a point to smile at every student.
It’s available to any teacher who guards their heart and mind against negativity, animosity, and resentment. It’s a choice, not a skill.
